summary: One LangChain ChatAnthropic call (@langchain/anthropic 1.5.12 on @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.122.0, model claude-sonnet-5-5 at $2/$10 per MTok, json_schema structured output, thinking between_tools = no reasoning in a tool-less call, effort low, no sampling override, SDK retries off, no prompt caching) turns a brief into Czech copy, a 1-7 slide deck and picture choices by sha256. The system prompt marketing-copy/5 is 6,068 bytes: 18 rule lines (4,103 bytes) plus the Humanizer embed (1,964 bytes of a 2,500 cap); the wire schema adds 1,980 bytes. Every checked figure of the owner brief section 2.4 matches the code (2 attempts, 20,000/2,500 tokens, $0.25 per job, $1.00 per 24 h, 45 s worker cap, offer 6 excerpts/12 media shrinking to 1/3/400, hashtags 8+5 capped at 10, caption 300-700 aim/1,500 schema/2,200 final, ~$0.02 expected and ~$0.11 worst per post). Measured on the test brief: $0.0229 expected per post, $0.0536 reserved per attempt, $0.107 worst for two attempts; the $0 studio fit gate takes 23-98 ms per deck; 62 generation/budget/humanizer/tracing tests pass in 1.4 s. The costliest defects are not dollars but input quality: the one-token-per-byte reservation silently cuts a rich brief from 6 sources/12 pictures/4,997 excerpt characters to 5/8/2,398 although the real prompt (~6,100 tokens) fits the 20,000-token budget three times over; the model never sees pictures although 12 thumbnails would cost $0.006; a clipped field costs a whole paid re-generation (~$0.026, ~half the call) instead of a targeted fix; a returned post has no regenerate path; and every provider error or timeout is booked as $0.25 against a $1.00 day, so four outages at $0 real cost close the day. Monthly model cost at 4 posts/day is about $2.75-3.80 on Sonnet 5.5 (worst case $12.90, ceiling-bounded at $30) or about $0.14 on Haiku 5.5; vision thumbnails add about $0.76/month; prompt caching would save under $0.01 per post at this volume and only pays on retries or batched runs. Verification (22 Oct): every cited line re-read on 8df25a5 and the reader's measurement script re-run with identical results; production SELECT shows 4 briefs (1 evidence each, 0-2 media, 137-236 excerpt chars), 0 jobs, 0 DNESKAi revisions and 0 generation spend rows, so every cost and latency figure is still an estimate.

findings.title: One-token-per-byte accounting silently cuts half the evidence and a third of the pictures of a rich brief
findings.claim: The offer is shrunk to fit 7,404 bytes because the 20,000-token budget is spent as bytes, so a 6-source/12-picture brief loses 52 % of its excerpt text and 4 of 12 pictures before the model sees it, although its real prompt (~6,100 tokens) fits the budget three times over. The brief's weak point 1 ('thin input') is partly manufactured here.

findings.title: Register and hook rules live only in prompt text that a test pins by hash; no gate checks them

findings.title: The number gate matches substrings, so invented numbers hidden in the date or other figures pass
findings.claim: supportedNumber uses corpus.includes(number) and the corpus contains the Czech target date, so '20', '10', '26', '2', '0' or '202' are 'supported' by '20. 10. 2026' and any digit run inside a longer number passes; the owner's hard rule is never to invent numbers.
findings.recommendation: Extract numbers from the corpus with the same regex into a set (normalising comma/point and Czech thousands spaces), exclude the target date and publication dates from that set, and require whole-token matches; add a test with '20 %' against a corpus containing '20. 10. 2026'.
findings.impactStatement: A fabricated '20 %' or '10 milionů' in a caption passes the only automated truth gate on numbers; the owner must catch it by eye in review. Low probability per post, high cost when it ships.

truth.evidence: dneskai-generation.ts:233 puts czechDate(targetDate) ("22. 10. 2026") into the corpus; :292-295 match by substring; :363 applies it to every text field. Tested here with the exact regex and function against a corpus "22. 10. 2026" + "150 milionů": "20 %", "2", "15", "50" and "202" all pass as supported; only "1,5" failed.

impact.reason: The only automated guard for the owner's hard rule on invented numbers lets common invented figures through; whole-token matching is a small, testable fix.

findings.title: Prompt caching is absent; at four posts a day it would save under a cent per post and only on retries or batched runs
findings.claim: The stable prefix (system + schema ≈ 2,683 tokens) is five times Sonnet 5.5's 512-token minimum, and the pinned LangChain forwards cache_control, but jobs run one per 5-minute tick, so the 5-minute cache mostly expires between posts: write premium ≈ $0.0013 per cold call, read saving ≈ $0.0048 per hit. If enabled, cost() would overcharge because LangChain folds cache reads into input_tokens.

evidence.excerpt: try { result = await traceable(() => structured.invoke([["system", input.system], ["human", input.prompt]], { signal: input.signal, callbacks: [] }), { tracingEnabled: false })(); }
No prompt caching, browsing, model tools, fallback provider or LLM judge participates.

findings.recommendation: Do not add it now. When variants or a vision pre-pass multiply calls per post, put cache_control on the system block, keep the rules stable and the voice/offer after the breakpoint, read usage_metadata.input_token_details for the ledger and record cache_read in the trace; assert cache_read_input_tokens > 0 in the A/B run.
findings.impactStatement: Net effect at today's volume is about $0 (−$0.0048 per retry, +$0.0013 per cold post); it becomes worth it only when several calls per post share the prefix (variants, vision pre-pass, A/B batches: 20 briefs back-to-back ≈ −$0.09 of a $0.46 run).

truth.evidence: generation.ts:457 sends plain string messages without cache_control; docs/marketing-generation.md:13 states no prompt caching; pinned @langchain/anthropic 1.5.12 forwards cache_control (chat_models.js:823, checked in the own-dashboard-fixes node_modules, same version; the audit worktree has no node_modules) and folds cache reads into input_tokens (utils/message_outputs.js:191), which generation.ts:176 would price at full rate. Prefix 2,683 tokens re-measured (bytes/3 estimate).

impact.reason: The finding itself recommends not acting at today's volume; revisit only with variants or batched calls.

The call profile for Haiku is ready, but the only planned use is the A/B after 20 approved posts; the pipeline has no second stage where a cheap model could take the low-judgement work (clip fixes, alt texts, picture ranking, hashtag proposals).

- [ ] **Run the DNESKAi model A/B after 20 approved posts** — once 20 DNESKAi posts are approved, and only with your consent to the spend, run `scripts/dneskai-model-ab.ts`

Run the A/B as planned; the 20-post gate is about five days at four posts a day.

impact.ownerDecision: Spend approval for Haiku stages and the planned A/B.
impact.reason: Dollar savings are a few dollars a month; the value only appears together with GEN-02/GEN-03, so it is an enabler, not a priority.

findings.title: Three nested deadlines (43 s tick minimum, 45 s generation, 55 s job) make the second attempt likely to time out and be booked as $0.25
findings.claim: Both attempts, the studio gate and media downloads must fit 45 s; a non-streaming Sonnet answer of ~1,500 tokens plausibly takes 15-25 s (not measured; nothing has run live), so a retry started after ~25 s is cut by the abort, and an abort during invoke runs ambiguous() before generation-timeout, booking the job maximum.

evidence.excerpt: collection: 20_000, media: 25_000, briefs: 5_000, generation: 43_000, publishing: 15_000, reconciliation: 5_000, token: 16_000,

findings.recommendation: Measure attempt latency in the pilot trace (latency_ms is already recorded); if a retry does not fit, persist the retry feedback on the job and run attempt 2 on the next tick instead of inside the same 45 s, or move the fix to the cheap Haiku rewrite (GEN-03). Longer term, give generation its own longer-running unit rather than a slice of the 60 s tick.
findings.impactStatement: A clipped post can lose its slot and $0.25 of the daily ceiling to a timeout rather than to a bad answer; the generation step also runs only when collection/media/briefs leave 43 s, which on a busy tick delays the 08:00 post (brief 2.10.5).

truth.evidence: Code confirmed: generation.ts:358 abort at maxLatencyMs, worker-runtime.ts:308 sets 45 s, :269 55 s job, scheduler.ts:75 generation needs 43 s, :53 hard stop 53 s; in generation.ts:383-386 an abort during invoke runs ambiguous() (booking $0.25) before throwing generation-timeout. That the second attempt is "likely" to time out rests on an unmeasured 15-25 s latency estimate; nothing has run live (0 jobs in production).

impact.reason: Real risk that compounds GEN-04, but it should be measured in the pilot trace before redesigning the deadlines.

findings.title: services/marketing-worker/README.md and docs describe an external n8n-called worker that needs a template; generation runs in-process from the pg_cron tick and DNESKAi jobs carry no template
findings.claim: The README says n8n Cloud calls the HTTP interface, hosting is unprovisioned and every job includes 'the exact approved template'; the code runs executeMarketingJob inside the tick, DneskaiDeckJobRequestSchema has no template, and the brief records n8n as idle with all timers on pg_cron.

evidence.excerpt: Hosting has not been provisioned or verified for this service. n8n Cloud calls this HTTP interface; it cannot run `ExecuteCommand` or use native workflow LangSmith tracing.
